nodes.name: Corollary 17
nodes.statement:
Let $c\leq d_{k,\ell} \in \mathbb{R}$ such that either 1)~$\tau_{k,\ell}$ is
    released before $c$, i.e., $c \geq r_{k,\ell}$ or 2)~$c < r_{k,\ell}$ and task $\tau_k$ is active during
        $[c,r_{k,\ell})$.
		If 
		\begin{equation}
			\widetilde{R}_{k,\ell} \!:=\!
			(C_k+ S_k) + \!\sum_{i \neq k}\! B^i_{k,\ell}(c,d_{k,\ell}) + \!\sum_{j < \ell}\! B_{k,j}(c,d_{k,\ell}) + c - r_{k,\ell},
		\end{equation}
		is at most $D_k$, then $\widetilde{R}_{k,\ell}$ is an upper bound on the response time of $\tau_{k,\ell}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 19, Lemma 22: Bounds for $B_{k,j}$ $\to$ B1 $B^i_{k,\ell}$ $\to$ B2
Theorem 23: Fixed analysis window
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbb{T} = \{\tau_1,\dots.\tau_n\}$ be an arbitrary-deadline task set with relative priority points $(\Pi_1, \dots, \Pi_n)$.
		If for all $k=1, \dots, n$ there exists some $b_k \in [0,D_k)$ such that
		\begin{equation}

			\widetilde{R}_k(b_k)

			\leq D_k,
		\end{equation}
		where $\widetilde{R}_k(b_k):=\left\lceil{\frac{D_k-b_k}{T_k}}\right\rceil(C_k + S_k) + b_k + \sum\limits_{i\neq k} \max\left(\left\lceil{\frac{G_k^i+ \widetilde{R}_i-b_k}{T_i}}\right\rceil, 0\right) C_i$
		and 


		$G^i_k = \min(D_k-C_i, \Pi_k-\Pi_i)$,
		then the task set is schedulable by EL scheduling with the given relative priority points and the worst-case response time of $\tau_k$ is upper bounded by $\widetilde{R}_k := \widetilde{R}_k(b_k)$.
